To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the AlN filled TIMs were found to be more efficient than BN filled TIMs in terms of thermal performance of high power LEDs.
the thermal resistance of high power LED package can be reduced by 11.33% by filling the thermal paste with AlN ceramic particles.
the AlN TIM achieve the least LED junction temperature and total thermal resistance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an AlN filled thermal paste for high power LED thermal management.
the investigation of thermal properties of AlN filled TIM in a high power LED package.
the investigation of ceramic particles filled thermal pastes as a potential thermal interface material for high power LED applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AlN at a D 50 50  nm was able to achieve the lowest LED junction temperature of 39.01 °C and the total thermal resistance of only 11.34 K/W. The
AlN TIM with D 50 40 nm is found to be the most suitable material for thermal management of high power LEDs.
the AlN TIM with the particle size of D 50 0.1170 nm is the most efficient thermal interface material in terms of thermal resistance for a high power LED device.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, the thermal performance of the high power LEDs can be improved with the incorporation of ceramic particle filled TIM.
AlN filled TIM is the best candidate for thermal management of high power LED.
the AlN TIM at D 50 of 1170 nm can be a promising material to be considered for future high power LED applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AlN filled thermal paste is an effective thermal interface material (AlN-TIM) for high power LED thermal management and it can be used in the future LED packages.
the thermal resistance of the LED package can be reduced by using a TIM filled with AlN particles.
the thermal performance of the device can be enhanced by the use of high thermal conductivity filler in thermal paste.
